findings.title: An interrupted first --keep run leaves an empty days-1.json that blocks the table from then on
findings.where: src/arci/logs/cli.py:350-359 (_write_outputs creates an empty O_EXCL placeholder at the final path before staging)
findings.what: Before staging anything, _write_outputs creates an empty file at each new target, the table included (mode 0600). If the process dies by SIGTERM, SIGKILL or power loss between that point and os.replace, the final path keeps a 0-byte days-1.json. Python cleanup only runs for exceptions (KeyboardInterrupt is handled). On every later run kept.read reports that file as 'unreadable' and prints F24. Because 'With --keep, a table that could not be read is not replaced', no later --keep run ever writes the table, until the user finds and deletes the file. The full staged table is left behind as a .realornoise-* temporary file. This breaks record 0017 'Writing' (the file is written to a temporary name and moved into place) and the claim under 'One size limit' that 'The run therefore never leaves behind a table its own reader would refuse.' New --json, --markdown and --html targets get the same empty placeholders, so 'if any write fails, none of the requested files is left changed' also fails on a kill.

Run from /Users/ajay/Developer/.arci-worktrees/wt-v2-logs with HOME=<scratch>/home REALORNOISE_HOME= .venv/bin/python t2.py setup; .venv/bin/python t2.py kill (patches os.replace to SIGKILL the process, which stands in for a SIGTERM or kill during the write; exit 137); .venv/bin/python t2.py check. Observed: days-1.json exists, size 0, mode 0600, beside .realornoise-xxxx (5.7k, the complete staged table). Two more `--keep` runs each exit 2, print 'The kept day table could not be read or is not valid. It was not used.' and leave the size at 0. Expected: after an interrupted first write, either no days-1.json or a complete one, so the next --keep run writes the table.
findings.fix: Do not create placeholders at the final paths. Stage to mkstemp files and run the same-file check on the staged or resolved names, or use os.link or rename with RENAME_EXCL semantics for new files. Or at least have kept.read treat a 0-byte file as 'absent' so a later run can replace it. Remove stale .realornoise-* files from the table directory on the next successful write.

findings.title: Concurrent --keep runs silently lose the other run's kept days (no lock, no re-read before the merge)
findings.where: src/arci/logs/cli.py:186-190 and 307-312 (the table is read at the start and the merge is written at the end, with no lock)
findings.what: The merge uses the rows read at the start of the run. When two runs overlap, for example a Claude Code run (plugin) and a Codex run (skill) that share one table, the later writer replaces the file with its own merge and drops every row the other run added. The record says rows of a tool that was not requested 'stay as stored'. Here a whole tool's rows vanish with no notice, and those days cannot be recovered once the logs age out.
findings.reproduction: Script: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ajay-Developer-agent-reliability-ci/39ca2335-7a5a-47d9-a374-69d92a47e1d0/scratchpad/review24/kept/t7.py. Run: python t7.py setup; (python t7.py slow_claude &) (a Claude Code --keep run whose write is delayed by 3 s); sleep 1.5; python t7.py codex (a Codex --keep run, which writes the codex rows: 'B wrote tools: [codex]'); sleep 4; python t7.py final. Observed: 'final tools: [claude-code]', so the codex rows are gone and both runs exited 2 with no error. Expected: both tools' rows present, or the second writer refuses or retries.
findings.fix: Take an exclusive lock (fcntl.flock on a lock file in the table directory) around read-merge-write. Or re-read the table under the lock just before the write and merge against that, with the same pair and prune rules.

findings.title: --keep-dir with an empty value writes the table into the current directory
findings.what: An empty REALORNOISE_HOME is treated as unset, as record 0017 says. An empty --keep-dir value (for example `--keep-dir "$UNSET"` or `--keep-dir=`) is instead accepted and becomes os.path.abspath(""), the current directory. The table, which holds model names and daily counts, is then created there (for example inside a project repository) with no message. That is neither a usage error nor the default directory. The record does not allow an empty DIR, and the same empty value is handled the opposite way for the environment variable.

verdicts.title: An interrupted first --keep run leaves an empty days-1.json that blocks the table from then on
verdicts.evidence: Code: src/arci/logs/cli.py _write_outputs opens each missing target with O_CREAT|O_EXCL (mode 0600 for the table) before staging, and removes placeholders only in a finally block, which does not run on a signal kill. Reproduced with copies of the reviewer's harness in .../review24/verify-kept-table/ (t2.py with SIGKILL, and t2term.py with a real SIGTERM sent from the patched os.replace; HOME in scratch, env={} so the table goes under the scratch home). Both: exit 137/143, then .realornoise/ holds days-1.json size 0 mode 0600 next to .realornoise-xxxx (5.7k, the complete staged table). Two later `--keep` runs each exit 2 with F24 and the file stays 0 bytes. Separately confirmed that a 0-byte days-1.json is read as 'unreadable' and never replaced by --keep (exit 2, size 0). Record 0017 'Writing': 'The file is written to a temporary name in the directory and moved into place'; 0016/0017 'if any write fails, none of the requested files is left changed'; 'With --keep, a table that could not be read is not replaced'. Without the placeholder, os.replace is atomic and a kill could only leave a stray temp file, so the placeholder alone causes the permanent block. New --json/--markdown/--html targets get the same 0-byte leftover.
verdicts.fix: Do not create anything at the final path before the content is ready. Stage each output to a mkstemp file beside the target; install an existing target with os.replace and a new target with os.link(staged, target) (fails with EEXIST, so a case-folding or symlink alias of an already-installed new target is detected there and reported as the same-file error) followed by unlinking the staged name. Optionally remove stale .realornoise-* files on the next successful write. The reviewer's fallback of having kept.read treat a 0-byte file as absent conflicts with the record ('kept_table is absent only when the path does not exist; any other failure to open it is unreadable') and should not be used.

verdicts.title: Concurrent --keep runs silently lose the other run's kept days (no lock, no re-read before the merge)
verdicts.evidence: Reproduced with a copy of t7.py: setup; Claude Code --keep run with _write_outputs delayed 3 s in the background; 1.5 s later a Codex --keep run prints 'B wrote tools: ['codex']'; after both finish, 'final tools: ['claude-code']'. Both exited 2, nothing on stderr. The table is read at the start of run() (kept.read) and the merge is written at the end with no lock or re-read. The record does not mention concurrency, but its write rule says rows of a tool not requested 'stay as stored', and the loss is silent. Severity stays low: it needs two overlapping --keep runs sharing one table, and the dropped rows come back on the next run of that tool as long as its logs still hold those days; they are lost for good only when the overwritten capture was the last one before the logs aged out.
verdicts.fix: Hold an exclusive fcntl.flock on a lock file in the table directory across kept.read through the install, or at least take the lock just before the write, re-read the table under it and merge against the fresh rows under the same pair and prune rules. Add a test with two overlapping runs.

verdicts.title: Readers and context counts changed in 2.4.0, but the docs say only version names changed
verdicts.evidence:
I read the reviewer's t7_ctx.py and gen.py, which write only under the scratch measures/work directory. I ran it from the review24/measures directory with HOME and REALORNOISE_HOME set to scratch, using the worktree venv, once with `old` (v2.3.0 source) and once with `new`.

With the same three Claude responses, the outputs differ:
- 2.3.0: client_versions_after 1, subagent_share_after '0/1'.
- 2.4.0: client_versions_after 3, subagent_share_after '1/3', client_versions_after_shown ['2.1.325', '2.1.321', '2.1.309'].

The code confirms the mechanism:
- claude_code.py now has `model_names`/`effort_names` parameters (lines 38-43) and collects `file_unconfigured` responses (lines 47-114).
- measures.py line 35 says unconfigured responses stay out of the response count, and lines 265-272 add `result.unconfigured_responses` to the context population.

The new behaviour is correct. It matches the definition in 0016 lines 228-230 and 0017 lines 201-202 and 599-601: context counts are taken "before the main-thread and setting filters". So 2.3.0 gave too-low F7 counts whenever a response lacked a setting.

Three documents still describe the readers as unchanged apart from version names:
- LOG_FORMATS.md lines 11-14: "In 2.4.0 the only reader change is client-version names ... Response assembly, duplicate handling, filtering, counts and unreadable-file rules are unchanged."
- 0017 "What 0017 leaves unchanged" lists "the readers, their counters and every reading fault" as unchanged from 0016. Its only reader change is the version-name tuple (lines 209-220).
- The CHANGELOG v2.4.0 Changed and Fixed entries do not mention the readers or the context counts.

The statement in LOG_FORMATS is false as written, because readers now also return setting-less responses and accept kept-name seeding. The record's "readers unchanged" line is also inaccurate. This is a documentation defect only: it causes no data loss, leak or crash, and the numbers are now right. The reviewer's severity of low is correct.
verdicts.fix:
Keep the code; it matches the 0016/0017 definition. Make three documentation changes:
- **LOG_FORMATS.md:** say that readers now also return main-thread and sub-agent responses without a model or effort. These responses count only toward the context counts (F7 and the F26 version list), never toward responses or day values. Also say that readers accept model and effort names taken from the kept table, so ids stay stable.
- **CHANGELOG v2.4.0, under "Fixed":** say that 2.3.0 left responses without a setting out of the context counts, against the 0016 definition, so `client_versions_*`, `workdirs_*` and `subagent_share_*` can be higher in 2.4.0 for the same logs.
- **Record 0017:** move "the readers" out of the unchanged list, or note this exception next to the version-name change. 0017 is under docs/design/**, which is frozen and needs the orchestrator's sign-off; if it cannot be edited, say so instead of working around it.

findings.title: The privacy suite's JSON string walk lets version-shaped strings through in any field, and its synthetic logs never contain a version that matches the pattern
findings.where: tests/unit/logs/privacy/test_json_leaves.py:40-66 (model_name, allowed) and tests/unit/logs/synth_logs.py:73,112 (only cli_version/version value is "98234567.76543210")

The allowance is written with that field scope. But allowed() also accepts any string that passes the model grammar in every field, and the model grammar accepts any version whose parts have at most two digits (2.1.30, 10.2.3, 0.15.0). The threat model cites test_every_json_string_leaf as the check of the JSON string categories, but it does not check that versions stay in their field. review.covered:
I found no leak in the product. No log string reached stdout, stderr, the Markdown, JSON or HTML files, the kept table, error lines or written file names, apart from the three bounded kinds of name. No socket or process was observed and no unrequested file was written.

What I attacked, with hostile synthetic logs built under scratchpad/review24/privacy (gen.py, gen2.py, runner.py with an audit hook):
- Secrets, ANSI and OSC escapes, `<script>` and javascript: Markdown, RTL marks, NUL bytes, CR and LF, and 5,000-character strings. I put them into cwd, message ids, sessionId, uuid, gitBranch, text and thinking blocks, tool_use input, tool_result content, unknown line types, non-JSON lines, invalid UTF-8, Codex session ids, originator, instructions, response_item and agent_message payloads, and keys of the usage object. The log directory and file names carried the secret too.
- Look-alike client versions: trailing newline or space, fullwidth, Arabic-Indic and mathematical digits, RLM, NUL, five parts, six-digit parts, 9.8.7654321. Look-alike model ids and efforts: newline, fullwidth or Arabic digit, uppercase, NUL, RLM, Cyrillic i, the secret itself, `<b>`.

Results:
- render_model and version_name use fullmatch with [0-9] and [a-z] and reject all of these. MODEL_WORDS matches the record exactly. A rejected model id cannot collide with a model-N or effort-N alias.
- All four outputs and the table hold only closed values, dates, fractions, hashes, claude-opus-5-5, gpt-5-codex, high, and versions 2.1.325, 2.1.321, 2.1.309 under client_versions_after_shown only. The text holds no control characters and no non-ASCII except the middle dot. The HTML has no script, href, src or url(), and every value goes through html.escape.
- A user --model value carrying an escape is never echoed. Bad --since, output into a missing directory and output under a file all print only fixed lines.
- Malformed input: 200,000-deep nesting, a 5,000-digit integer, lone surrogates, a chmod 000 file, a FIFO and a directory named .jsonl, a dangling symlink, a symlink loop, and corrupt and truncated .zst files under Python 3.14 and 3.13. These give only counts or fixed lines, with no traceback, path or file name.
- A hostile kept table (model containing the secret and ESC) prints F24 only and is left byte for byte under --keep-dir.

Write and process boundary:
- Audit-hook runs show: no socket or subprocess events, including the import of arci.cli. A run without --keep and without outputs writes nothing, even with a table present. --example --keep writes no table and creates no directory. --keep creates the directory with 0700 and writes days-1.json with 0600, through .realornoise-* temporary files. With an existing table it also makes a temporary backup copy, which is removed on success.
- The plugin skill and the Codex skill each run one pinned command, uvx --python 3.14 realornoise==2.4.0, and say that the printed counts, rates, dates and bounded names enter the conversation.
